parts.text:
**Medi-Cal** is California’s Medicaid program, providing free or low-cost health care coverage to low-income individuals, including families, seniors, people with disabilities, children, and pregnant individuals. 

Due to state and federal legislative changes, several major rules regarding eligibility, asset limits, and enrollment have changed. 

---

### 1. Crucial 2026 Policy Changes (Urgent Updates)
If you are planning to apply for Medi-Cal or are currently enrolled, there are several key updates you must be aware of:

*   **Asset Limits Have Been Reinstated (Effective January 1, 2026):** 
    For seniors (65+), individuals with disabilities, and those requiring long-term care, California has reinstated the asset test. 
    *   **The Limit:** You can own up to **$130,000** in countable assets as an individual. You can add **$65,000** for each additional household member (up to 10 people).
    *   **What Counts:** Bank accounts, cash, secondary properties, and certain vehicles.
    *   **What is Exempt:** Your primary home, one vehicle, and personal household items are generally not counted.
*   **Enrollment Freeze for Undocumented Adults (Effective January 1, 2026):**
    *   **New Applicants:** Undocumented adults (ages 19 and older who are not pregnant) can no longer newly enroll in full-scope Medi-Cal. New applications will only qualify for restricted-scope Medi-Cal (covering emergency, pregnancy-related, and long-term nursing care).
    *   **Existing Enrollees:** If you are already enrolled in full-scope Medi-Cal, **you will keep your full-scope coverage as long as you complete your annual renewal on time.** If your coverage lapses, you only have 90 days to resolve the paperwork; after that, you will not be allowed to re-enroll in full-scope coverage.
    *   **Exceptions:** Children (ages 0–18) and pregnant/postpartum individuals can still newly enroll in full-scope Medi-Cal regardless of immigration status.
*   **Dental Reductions (Effective July 1, 2026):** Undocumented adults (19+, non-pregnant) will have full dental benefits reduced to **emergency dental coverage only**.
*   **Upcoming Work Requirements (Effective January 1, 2027):** Under federal legislation (H.R. 1), certain working-age adults (ages 19–64) on Medi-Cal will need to meet work, school, or community service requirements to keep their coverage. Exemptions will apply for caregivers of children under 14, people with disabilities, and those who are medically frail.

---

### 2. General Eligibility Requirements
To qualify for Medi-Cal, you must be a resident of California and meet certain financial requirements:

*   **Income Limits:** For most adults (ages 19–64), your household income must be at or below **138% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL)**. 
    *   *For example, in 2026, 138% FPL is approximately $20,783 per year for an individual, or $43,056 for a family of four (these numbers adjust slightly each year).*
    *   Children, pregnant individuals, and certain disabled individuals qualify under higher income thresholds.

---

### 3. What Does Medi-Cal Cover?
Medi-Cal covers a wide range of "Essential Health Benefits," which are generally free or very low-cost:

*   **Medical Care:** Routine doctor visits, preventative care, vaccines, specialist visits, and emergency room/hospital stays.
*   **Prescription Drugs (Medi-Cal Rx):** Under updated 2026 guidelines, weight-loss drugs are not covered, and over-the-counter (OTC) items (including COVID-19 rapid tests) now require prior authorization.
*   **Mental Health:** Therapy, counseling, and substance use disorder treatments.
*   **Dental Care (Denti-Cal):** Screenings, cleanings, x-rays, fillings, and root canals (note the restricted emergency-only dental coverage for undocumented adults starting July 2026).
*   **Vision Care:** Eye exams and glasses.
*   **Maternity and Newborn Care:** Complete prenatal, delivery, and postpartum care.

---

### 4. How to Apply
You can apply for Medi-Cal at any time of the year (there is no closed enrollment period):

1.  **Online (Fastest):** Apply through [CoveredCA.com](https://www.coveredca.com/) or [BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com/). The system will automatically check if you qualify for Medi-Cal.
2.  **By Phone:** Call Covered California at **1-800-300-1506** or contact your local county social services agency.
3.  **In Person / Mail:** Visit your local county social services office to pick up, turn in, or mail an application.

**Documents you may need to apply:**
*   Proof of identity (ID, driver's license).
*   Proof of residency in California (utility bill, rental agreement).
*   Proof of income (tax returns, W-2s, or recent pay stubs).
*   Immigration documents (if applicable).
*   Proof of assets (bank statements, property documents, if subject to the asset test).

### 5. Crucial: Keep Your Information Up to Date
Because of the strict renewal laws now in place, **always make sure your county social services office has your correct mailing address, phone number, and email**. When you receive your yellow renewal envelope in the mail, fill it out and return it immediately to avoid losing your coverage.
